reference: Carvajal, E., Montes, L., Almanza, O.A. (2011) Quaternary dating by electron spin resonance (ESR) applied to human tooth enamel. Earth Sciences Research Journal 15(2), 115-120.

conventions.gamma_source: computed by ROSY from soil U/Th/K (Table 1); soil density 2.00, enamel 3.00, dentine 2.82 g/cm3

samples.provenance: Table 1 (soil gamma spectrometry, p. 118), Table 2 (ROSY dose-rate components, p. 118); De, thicknesses, densities, water and cosmic from text pp. 117-118
samples.notes: Human tooth from a collective burial, Aguazuque archaeological site (Cundinamarca, Colombia; savannah near Bogota). Age printed as 3,256 +- 190 y BP, converted to ka; text says EU, LU and CU gave the same age. U, Th, K in enamel and dentine were NOT measured (assumed negligible) -> internal and dentine dose = 0. Table 1 prints soil 40K as '1.66 +- 0.09 ppm'; Table 2 contains no K contribution (sum of U and Th terms + cosmic = total exactly), so K appears not to have contributed in the published calculation -- treat with care. Dose components are self-consistent: 34.54+12.01 = 46.55; 188.50+158.81 = 347.31; 46.55+347.31+251 = 644.86; 2.10 Gy / 644.86 uGy/a = 3.256 ka. The 'Sediment (alpha+beta)' label in Table 2 corresponds to the U+Th beta sum. | Curation: gamma_uGy_a set to null because the paper computes gamma with ROSY from the same soil analysis; EPRdating recomputes it (the published value stays under published.dose_rates_uGy_a.gamma_sediment). | Curation: K_pct = 0 reproduces the published calculation (no K contribution); see K_as_printed_ppm. | Verified: Table 1 column '40K' under 'Concentration (ppm)', 1.66 ± 0.09; 1.66 ppm of 40K is ~1.42 % K. Table 2 has an explicit 'Potassium' row of 0.00. Removed layer printed 'about 50±5 mm' (acid etching), evidently µm.

completeness: partial: tooth U/Th/K not measured (assumed zero); no k or 234U/238U (irrelevant with zero U); otherwise complete with thicknesses, removed layers, water, densities and full dose-rate breakdown
extraction_notes: Read twice via WebFetch with consistent numbers. Page range 115-120 confirmed. Site coordinates printed as "40° 37' North and 74°17' West" (latitude evidently a typo, Bogota savannah is ~4.6°N) -- not entered as lat/lon. A useful ROSY external-dose test case (thick enamel 1.4 mm, dentine 5 mm, 50 um stripped each side).
benchmark_reason: external dose only: tooth U/Th/K not measured (zero in the paper)
